content: Patients taking this medication may experience kidney-related side effects, such as increased creatinine levels, protein in the urine (proteinuria), and excessive urination (polyuria). General side effects may include weakness or fatigue (asthenia). Severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B have been reported in patients co-infected with HIV-1 and hepatitis B virus (HBV) after discontinuing this medication. Bone loss and defects in bone mineralization have also been observed. Lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (fatty liver) have been reported with the use of this drug, either alone or in combination with other antiretroviral medications. If a patient develops clinical or laboratory findings suggestive of lactic acidosis or significant hepatotoxicity (which may include hepatomegaly and steatosis even without elevated liver enzymes), treatment should be immediately discontinued. Before initiating antiretroviral therapy, patients with HIV-1 should be tested for chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. If HBV is present, starting anti-hepatitis B therapy may be necessary, particularly in patients with advanced liver disease or cirrhosis, as stopping treatment can lead to severe hepatitis exacerbations, potentially resulting in liver failure. Fat redistribution and accumulation have been observed in patients undergoing antiretroviral therapy. A pregnancy registry has been established to monitor outcomes in pregnant individuals exposed to antiretroviral medications (Antiviral Pregnancy Registry: 1-800-258-4263). However, current data from the registry are insufficient to fully assess the risk of birth defects or miscarriage. This medication is not recommended during pregnancy due to significantly reduced levels of cobicistat and elvitegravir during the second and third trimesters. Pregnant individuals should consider alternative treatment regimens. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advises against breastfeeding for HIV-infected mothers due to the risk of postnatal HIV transmission. Limited data indicate that emtricitabine and tenofovir are present in human breast milk, but it is unknown whether elvitegravir or cobicistat are excreted in human milk. However, these two drugs have been detected in the milk of lactating rats. Mothers should be instructed not to breastfeed due to the potential for HIV transmission (in HIV-negative infants), the development of viral resistance (in HIV-positive infants), and adverse reactions in breastfed infants similar to those seen in adults. Elvitegravir is an integrase inhibitor that blocks the catalytic activity of HIV-1 integrase, an enzyme essential for viral replication. It is metabolized by CYP3A4. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and acts as a pharmacokinetic enhancer, boosting the systemic exposure of CYP3A substrates like elvitegravir by reducing their metabolism. Emtricitabine is a synthetic nucleoside analog of cytidine, which inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with natural substrates and causing chain termination when incorporated into viral DNA. Tenofovir is an acyclic nucleoside phosphonate analog of adenosine monophosphate, which inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with deoxyadenosine triphosphate and terminating DNA synthesis. Food increases the systemic exposure of elvitegravir and tenofovir by 34% and 24%, respectively. A high-fat meal (~800 kcal, 50% fat) further increases their systemic exposure by 87% and 23%, respectively. This medication is marketed under the brand name Stribild. It is used to control HIV infection by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, allowing the immune system to function more effectively. This reduces the risk of HIV-related complications (e.g., new infections, cancer) and improves quality of life. However, it is not a cure for HIV. Patients should continue taking all HIV medications as prescribed and use effective barrier methods (e.g., condoms, dental dams) during sexual activity to prevent spreading HIV to others. Personal items that may come into contact with blood or body fluids (e.g., needles, toothbrushes, razors) should not be shared. Patients should take this medication exactly as prescribed. It should be taken at least 2 hours before or after other products that may interfere with its effectiveness. For optimal results, doses should be evenly spaced. Patients should not alter their dosage or stop taking the medication without consulting their doctor. Common side effects include diarrhea, headache, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, unusual dreams, back pain, and changes in skin color on the palms or soles. As the immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms to reappear. In rare cases, the immune system may become overactive, leading to symptoms at any time during treatment. Rarely, this medication can cause severe (and sometimes fatal) liver and blood problems, such as lactic acidosis. Tenofovir may increase the risk of bone loss. Patients at risk for bone loss may require monitoring of bone mineral density and supplementation with calcium and vitamin D. Patients should inform their doctor of any allergies or other medications they are taking, as drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of side effects. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control, increasing the risk of pregnancy. Patients should discuss alternative birth control methods with their doctor. If an overdose occurs, seek emergency medical attention immediately. Routine laboratory tests (e.g., kidney and liver function, hepatitis B testing, viral load, T-cell counts, blood mineral levels, bone density tests, urine glucose/protein) should be conducted before and during treatment. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. This summary does not include all possible information about this product. Patients should consult their healthcare provider for complete details tailored to their specific health needs.
